description:
Make a matching, seamlessly tiling texture SET for a material: a colour map, a normal map and a packed ambient-occlusion / roughness / metalness map, rendered by R3 from a procedural recipe (seeded noise, stones, bricks …). Nothing is uploaded and it is free. The maps are stored as images in the account (the owner sees them in the Images browser as "<name> · albedo.png" …).

Start from a preset (gravel, sand, concrete, bricks) with optional controls: seed (another variation), scale (an integer: finer pattern), colours (the ramp's "#rrggbb" stops), contrast, bumpiness (normal strength), roughness {min, max}, size (256 / 512 / 1024 / 2048, default 1024), tileWorldSize (metres one tile covers, default 1), height (also store a 16-bit height map). Or pass a full `recipe` (r3_docs_read("TEXTURE_RECIPES.md") has the format and every preset's recipe). An invalid recipe is refused with the path of the problem.

Pass `apply` {projectId, material, repeat | worldSize} to put it on a material in the same call (as r3_texture_apply). You cannot see the texture: the answer gives numbers (mean colour, brightness range, height spread, seam check) and the colour map's url; r3_editor_capture shows it in an open editor. Names are unique per account. Each call makes a NEW set; reuse a set with r3_texture_apply.

apply.description: Also wire it to a material: {projectId, material, repeat | worldSize}.

material.description: The material to wire: its entityRef or id (r3_project_load), e.g. "material_ground".

repeat.description: How often the texture repeats across the surface (the same on every map). Default 1.

worldSize.description: Or: the surface size in metres; repeat = worldSize / the set's tile size (1 m for the presets), e.g. 1000 for a 1 km terrain.

controls.description: With a preset: {seed, scale, colours, contrast, bumpiness, roughness: {min, max}, size, tileWorldSize, height}.

name.description: What the owner sees, e.g. "Gravel path". Unique in the account.

preset.description: A preset: gravel, sand, concrete, bricks.

name: r3_texture_create

answer.description: This answer in words: what was done, what R3 measured, decided or refused, and what to do next. The same text as the result's text block. Read it: the fields beside it are the data, this is the guidance.

title: Make a tileable texture set (colour, normal, roughness) from a recipe
